decks.name: LeetCode #79 - Word Search
decks.description: Search for a word in a 2D board using backtracking with adjacent cells

cards.question: Word Search: Given an m x n grid of characters board and a string word, return true if word exists in the grid. The word can be constructed from letters of sequentially adjacent cells, where adjacent cells are horizontally or vertically neighboring. The same letter cell may not be used more than once.

solutions.name: Backtracking (Hash Set)
solutions.explanation: Use DFS backtracking with hash set to track visited cells. Start DFS from every cell in board. Base case when index equals word length (found complete word). Return false if out of bounds, character mismatch, or cell already visited. Add current cell to path set, recursively explore all 4 directions, then remove from set (backtrack). Hash set provides O(1) lookup for visited cells. Try all starting positions until word found or all exhausted. O(m*4^n) time where m is board cells and n is word length.

solutions.name: Backtracking (Visited Array)
solutions.explanation: Use DFS backtracking with 2D boolean array to track visited cells. Similar to hash set approach but uses array indexing instead of set operations. Initialize visited array with all false. Mark cell as visited before exploring neighbors, mark as unvisited during backtrack. Array access is O(1) and may have better cache locality than hash set. Same time complexity but different space representation. Good when board dimensions known and reasonable size. O(m*4^n) time with O(m+n) space for visited array and recursion stack.

solutions.spaceDescription: Visited array takes O(m) space for all board cells, recursion stack depth up to n, but m is typically much smaller than 4^n output so O(n) dominates
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given board=[['A','B','C','E'],['S','F','C','S'],['A','D','E','E']], word='ABCCED': Start at (0,0)='A'. Set visited[0][0]=true. Match 'B' at (0,1), set visited[0][1]=true. Continue matching path through board. When complete word found at (2,1)='D', return true. Visited array prevents cycles during search, gets reset during backtracking for other paths.

solutions.name: Backtracking (Optimal)
solutions.explanation: Use DFS backtracking by modifying board in-place instead of separate tracking structure. Mark visited cells by temporarily replacing character with '#'. Before exploring neighbors, save original character and replace with '#'. After exploring, restore original character during backtrack. Most space efficient as no extra data structure needed. Board modification is safe since we restore values. Only recursion stack space required. Same O(m*4^n) time complexity but O(n) space only for recursion stack, no additional tracking structure. Best space efficiency.
